chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Feeding one child is not sufficient for the expiation of an oath, but rather two children are equivalent to one adult.

key_terms.كَفَّارَةِ: Expiation (atonement for a sin or broken oath)

ai.seo_question: How many children count as one adult for expiating an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the quantitative measure for feeding the poor in expiation (kaffarah) of an oath, establishing that two children are equivalent to one adult. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of precise legal quantification, ensuring the obligation is fulfilled with sufficient sustenance rather than a mere symbolic gesture. It underscores the importance of equitable distribution in religious duties, linking the physical act of feeding to the spiritual intent of atonement.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘It is not sufficient, feeding the young with regards to an expiation of the oath, but two young and an old one’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said
in paying expiation for an oath, feeding small people is not sufficient, however, two small ones are equal to one grown-up person.”’
